verses: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَدْحًا فَمُلَٰقِيهِ
وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِىَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ وَرَآءَ ظَهْرِهِۦ
بَلَىٰٓ إِنَّ رَبَّهُۥ كَانَ بِهِۦ بَصِيرًا
وَإِذَا قُرِئَ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقُرْءَانُ لَا يَسْجُدُونَ
إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ لَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍۭ

leads.title: Michael arises, the resurrection, and the sealed book ↔ The splitting: the book in the right hand
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God keeps a book in which names are written and from which sinners are blotted (weight 5.4). Pair score 5.4.

Only in Michael arises, the resurrection, and the sealed book: Two figures stand on either bank of the river, with a linen-clad figure above the waters; Secret reckonings: 1,290 days from the abolition of the daily offering, and blessed is he who waits for 1,335 days; Many shall run to and fro and knowledge shall increase; The seer is told he will rest and rise to his allotted portion at the end of days; A time of trouble such as never was since nations existed; The wise shine like the brightness of the firmament and those who turn many to righteousness like the stars forever; On judgment day each receives a book of his deeds spread open, leaving nothing small or great unrecorded [divergence between the texts]; God raises his hand to heaven and swears: as I live forever; Into how many groups humankind is sorted at the end [divergence between the texts]; A heavenly being or the seer asks 'Until when (ad matai)?' the desolation will last; The resurrected cry 'Woe to us, who has raised us from our sleeping place (marqad)?'; Persecution lasts 'a time, times and half a time' (three and a half periods); and 8 more.

Only in The splitting: the book in the right hand: O man, you are toiling laboriously toward your Lord, and you will meet him; 'You will surely ride (pass through) stage upon stage' (tabaqan 'an tabaq); Whoever is given his book in his right hand has an easy reckoning; whoever is given it behind his back cries for destruction; Sky and earth 'listen to their Lord' (adhinat) and are made to obey at the end; Those who do not prostrate when the scripture is recited to them are rebuked (a prostration verse) [contrast between the texts]; Those who do not prostrate when the scripture is recited to them are rebuked (a prostration verse); At the end the earth is stretched out, casts out what is in it (its burdens) and empties itself; At the end the sky is split, cleft or opened (infatarat, inshaqqat, furijat); Oath introduced by the negated formula 'No! I swear by...' (la uqsimu / fa-la uqsimu); A series of oaths by natural phenomena (dawn, night, day, sun, moon, sky, earth, stars, winds) opens or punctuates a passage.
